  five steps have been completed, then the Special Tax shall be levied Proportionately on all Taxable
  Public Property at a rate up to 100% of the Maximum Special Tax for Taxable Public Property to
  satisfy the Annual Special Tax Requirement.

F.  APPEAL OF SPECIAL TAX LEVY
  Any property owner may file a written appeal of the Special Tax with the CFD Administrator claiming
  that the amount or application of the Special Tax is not correct with respect to one or more specific
  Assessor’s Parcels. The appeal must be filed not later than one calendar year after having paid the
  Special Tax that is disputed, and the appellant must be current in all payments of the Special Taxes
  theretofore levied on the Assessor’s Parcel(s). In addition, during the term of the appeal process,
  all Special Tax levied must be paid for the subject Assessor’s Parcel(s) prior to delinquency.
  The appeal must specify the reasons why the appellant claims the Special Tax is in error. The CFD
  Administrator shall review the appeal, meet with the appellant if the CFD Administrator deems
  necessary, and advise the appellant of its determination.
  If the property owner disagrees with the CFD Administrator’s decision relative to the appeal, the
  owner may then file a written appeal with the City Council whose subsequent decision shall be final
  and binding on all interested parties. If the decision of the CFD Administrator or subsequent
  decision by the City requires the Special Tax to be modified or changed in favor of the property
  owner, then an adjustment shall be made to credit future Special Taxes.
  This procedure shall be exclusive and its exhaustion by any property owner shall be a condition
  precedent to filing any legal action by such owner.

  adversely affect the levy and collection of Special Taxes on any Assessor’s Parcel needed to repay

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement No. A-8618 with Square Signs, LLC., dba Front Signs, for PN
  888, Street Sweeping Signage, for $391,150 for a term of 100 working days from
  the date of the Notice to Proceed; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8618
  with Square Signs, LLC., dba Front Signs, including minimal and/or non-
  substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

Palmdale Municipal Code 12.36, amended through Ordinance No. 1612, and adopted by
City Council on November 15, 2023, requires “No Parking” signage associated with street
sweeping days. Project No. 888 provides for the purchase and installation of “No Parking”
signs within the residential streets of Palmdale. The City is following Waste
Management’s trash collection schedule to maximize the benefits of street sweeping.
There are 18 sweeping zones that are identified in Attachment 1 and 2, and street
sweeping will be done twice a month on the first business day after a scheduled trash
pickup. (For example, Zone A & Q have trash pickup on Friday, so their street sweeping
days would be the first and third Monday of every month). The total number of “No
Parking” signs to be installed is 4,900.

DISCUSSION

On December 18, 2023, the project was advertised electronically through PlanetBids.
A total of thirteen (13) prospective bidders downloaded the bid documents.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Award of PN 888, Agreement No. A-8618
February 21, 2024
Page 2

On January 16, 2024, five (5) bids for this project were received, summarized, and listed
below:

  Bidder  Location  Amount
 1. Square Signs, LLC., dba Front Signs  Burbank, CA  $391,150.00
 2. Cal-Stripe, Inc.  Colton, CA  $469,485.00
 3. BC Traffic Specialist  Garden Grove, CA  $545,975.00
 4. PCI  Azusa, CA  $618,630.00
 5. Sterndahl Enterprises, LLC.  Sun Valley, CA  $708,756.00

The City received one bid protest from Cal-Stripe, Inc. The bid protest asserts, in part, the
following: Square Signs, LLC., dba Front Signs, is in possession of a C-45 license and
did not list subcontractors to perform the traffic control that this project may require, and
Cal-Stripe, Inc. stated that Square Signs, LLC., dba Front Signs, had discrepancies noted
in the reference form. Upon review of the bid documents and checking references, the
City has determined that the bid protest from Cal-Stripe, Inc. lacks merit and has informed
the contractor of this decision. Square Signs, LLC., dba Front Signs, was found to be the
lowest responsible, responsive bidder, and staff recommends awarding PN 888 to Square
Signs, LLC., dba Front Signs, for $391,150.

Once the signs are in place, enforcement will be handled by the City’s Code Enforcement
Division. A plan to educate the public through various channels, like social media,
newspapers, and community events, will be implemented before they start enforcement.

BACKGROUND

California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) Decision 22-05-015 (D. 22-05-015)
adopted a Modified Cost Allocation Mechanism (MCAM), Attachment 2, cost recovery
process for each investor-owned utility (IOU) that conducted procurement on behalf of
load-serving entities (LSEs) that opted out of their specific procurement obligations under
CPUC D.19-11-016. Unlike the traditional cost allocation mechanism, where all
customers in an IOU’s service territory cover procurement costs, under the MCAM, the
resource costs are recovered only from customers whose LSEs opted out of procurement.

D. 22-05-015 also adopted a one-time provision allowing non-IOU LSEs to negotiate
purchasing the portion of D.19-11-016 capacity that the IOU had procured on behalf of
customers who, after 2019, departed IOU service for purchasing LSE’s service.

Initially, EPIC was ineligible for the MCAM resource adequacy (RA) or electrical grid
reliability allocation under D. 22-05-015 due to the timing of its commencement of service
to customers.

However, in December of 2023, CPUC D. 23-12-014 granted San Diego Community
Power and Clean Energy Alliance’s Petition for Modification of the D. 22-05-015 on the
MCAM for Opt-Out and Backstop Procurement Obligations. This action afforded eligibility
to additional load-serving entities, including EPIC, to purchase resource adequacy
capacity through the MCAM.

Based on EPIC’s 2023 year-ahead load forecast and the 2023 year-ahead forecast for
SCE’s 2019 vintage departing load customers, SCE has calculated that EPIC’s share
eligible for purchase of the RA procured per D. 19-011-016 is 9.78 MW.

The opportunity for Palmdale to procure additional resource adequacy capacity under the
MCAM approach is financially advantageous to EPIC and its customers. To secure
resource adequacy capacity under the MCAM approach, EPIC must enter into a Master
Power Purchase and Sale Agreement with SCE by March 15, 2024, for inclusion in an
SCE advice letter filed to the CPUC on or before April 1, 2024.

DISCUSSION

The opportunity to participate in SCE’s MCAM offering aligns with State mandates and
EPIC’s resource adequacy procurement obligations to support overall grid resiliency in a
financially advantageous manner to EPIC and its customers.

FISCAL IMPACT

Sufficient revenues will be generated to cover the costs associated with the proposed
action.

The annual cost associated with EPIC’s MCAM allocation is estimated to be $1,787,393
beginning in 2025. This contract will displace the need to purchase the same amount of
resource adequacy from other sellers in the wholesale power market. The net fiscal
impact is expected to be beneficial in the near term and neutral in the longer term. The
price paid under this contract will be equivalent to the resource adequacy market price
benchmark adopted annually by the CPUC during the term of this agreement, which runs
through 2041.

This benchmark price for 2025 will initially be set by the CPUC in October of 2024 and
trued up in October of 2025 based on prevailing market conditions. This annual process
of updating the market price benchmark and contract price will continue and will be based

  RECITALS

  WHEREAS, the California Public Utilities Commission (“CPUC”) adopted the
Decision Granting Petition for Modification on Modified Cost Allocation Mechanism D.
23-12-014 on December 19, 2023;

  WHEREAS, D.23-12-014 provides load-serving entities with loads that migrated
from the investor-owned utilities based on the final 2023 resource adequacy year-ahead
forecast finalized in August 2022 the option to enter into an agreement with the relevant
investor-owned utility that conducted procurement in accordance with D.19-11-016 to
purchase a share of the system resource adequacy (“RA”) capacity at the Market Price
Benchmark calculated in accordance with the provisions of D.19-10-001;

  WHEREAS, Counterparty is a load-serving entity with such migrated loads and
desires to enter into this Agreement to purchase its eligible system RA share of SCE’s
D.19-11-016 procurement; and

  2.1  Seller’s Delivery Obligations

  identifying and confirming the transfer of the Expected Contract Quantity of
  Product to Buyer for each Showing Month (the “Supply Plan Obligation”).

  (b)  Showing Month Notice. If (i) Seller intends to utilize an Alternate Unit in
  accordance with Section 2.3 to satisfy its Supply Plan Obligation, or (ii)
  Seller intends to deliver less than the Contract Quantity of Product for such
  Showing Month for any reason, then Seller shall, or shall cause the Unit’s
  SC to, submit written notification to Buyer (the “Showing Month Notice”),
  no later than the Compliance Notification Deadline, identifying (x) such
  Alternate Unit(s) in accordance with Section 2.3, (y) the Contract Quantity
  of Product from such Alternate Unit(s), and (z) the total Contract Quantity
  to be provided on the Showing Month Supply Plan.

  (c)  Contract Quantity Unit Allocation. Seller may deliver Product from any one
  or combination of Unit(s) set forth in Appendix C at Seller’s sole discretion.
  Seller shall provide email notice to Buyer’s Supply Plan contact, as set forth
  in Appendix D, no later than the initial Compliance Showing Deadline for
  each Showing Month containing the allocation of Contract Quantity by Unit
  (“Contract Quantity Unit Allocation”).

  2.2  Adjustments to Contract Quantity

  Seller shall deliver to Buyer the Contract Quantity of Product for each Showing
  Month consistent with the following:

  (a)  Planned Outages: Seller’s obligation to deliver the Contract Quantity for
  each Showing Month may be reduced at Seller’s option by the amount of
  any Planned Outages which exist with respect to any portion of the Units
  listed in Appendix C during the applicable Showing Month. Seller shall
  notify Buyer no later than the Compliance Notification Deadline of the
  amount of Product from the Unit Buyer is permitted to include in Buyer’s
  Compliance Showings applicable to that month as a result of such Planned
  Outage.

  (b)  Reductions in Unit NQC and Unit EFC: Seller’s obligation to deliver the
  applicable Contract Quantity for each Showing Month may also be reduced
  in the event the Unit experiences a reduction in Unit NQC or Unit EFC after
  the Confirmation Effective Date as determined by the CAISO. In the event
  the Unit experiences such a reduction in Unit NQC or Unit EFC, Seller has
  the option, but not the obligation, to provide the applicable Contract
  Quantity for such Showing Month from (i) the same Unit, provided the Unit
  has sufficient remaining and available Product or (ii) from Alternate Units,
  provided, that in each case Seller provides and identifies such Alternate
  Units in accordance with Section 2.3.

  (c)  Reductions in Seller Supply: Seller’s obligation to deliver the applicable
  Contract Quantity for each Showing Month may also be reduced in the
  event that Unit(s) fail to deliver the Contracted Amount for any reason,
  including but not limited to (i) a delay in achieving commercial operation by
  the Unit(s); (ii) early termination of the Seller Supply Agreement; (iii)
  reduction in the Contracted Amount in the Seller Supply Agreement; (iv)
  planned maintenance of the Unit(s); and (v) a change in law resulting in a
  reduction of Unit NQC, Unit EFC, or the Capacity Attributes provided by
  the Unit(s). If there is a reduction in Seller’s supply in accordance with this
  Section 2.2(c), Seller has the option, but not the obligation, to provide the
  applicable Contract Quantity for such Showing Month from Alternate Units,
  provided, that in each case Seller provides and identifies such Alternate
  Units in accordance with Section 2.3.

  ARTICLE 3. PAYMENT

  3.1  Monthly Payment

  In accordance with the terms of Article Six of the Master Agreement, Buyer shall
  make a Monthly Payment to Seller, after the applicable Showing Month, as
  follows:

  Monthly Payment = (A x B x 1,000)

  where:

  A = applicable Contract Price for that Showing Month

  B = The amount of Contract Quantity of Product actually delivered by
  Seller to Buyer pursuant to and consistent with Section 2.1 and, if
  applicable, Section 2.3, for the applicable Showing Month.

  The Monthly Payment calculation shall be rounded to two decimal places. The
  Monthly Payment is subject to an annual true-up in accordance with Section 3.4.

  3.2  Allocation of Other Payments and Costs

  (a)  Seller shall retain any revenues it may receive from and pay all costs
  charged by the CAISO or any other third party with respect to the Unit for

  ancillary services, and (iv) black start or reactive power services.

  Contract Quantity (including any capacity revenues from RMR Contracts
  for the Unit, Capacity Procurement Mechanism or its successor, RUC

  shall cause each Unit’s SC to, submit RUC Availability Bids for the

  (c)  In accordance with Section 3.1 of this Confirmation and Article Six of the

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-011, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
  Palmdale authorizing the acceptance of the California Department of Justice
  Tobacco Grant Program funds in the amount of $793,710 and approving the
  related agreement for the term of November 1, 2023, through June 30, 2027; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager, or her designee, to execute the Agreement with the
  California Department of Justice Tobacco Grant Program and submit all
  documents, including, but not limited to, amendments and payment requests, as
  appropriate to accept the funds and comply with the conditions of the grant.

BACKGROUND

On July 10, 2018, the City of Palmdale adopted Resolution No. CC 2018-053,
authorizing the implementation of the City’s Tobacco Outreach and Enforcement
Program, and the acceptance of $435,000 from the California Department of Justice
Tobacco Grant Program (Tobacco Grant) and related Memorandum of Understanding
(A-6917), with a term of June 1, 2018, through June 30, 2020.

On April 7, 2020, the City accepted an additional allocation of $361,243 from the
California Department of Justice Tobacco Grant Program, with a term of July 1, 2020,
through June 30, 2022.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: California Department of Justice Tobacco Grant Program
February 21, 2024
Page 2

The City of Palmdale has seventy-eight (78) licensed tobacco retailers within its
jurisdiction. Tobacco Grant funds have been approved for enforcement, investigation,
compliance checks, and education of local tobacco laws and ordinances.

DISCUSSION

The approved allocation of funds for the enforcement program includes inspections of
randomly selected tobacco retailers and conducts a series of tobacco enforcement
sweeps to ensure compliance with local and state laws. The program provides an
innovative approach focused on enforcement, investigation, compliance, and education,
including the following goals:

● Identify and target problematic retailers of tobacco products.
● Conduct quarterly tobacco-related enforcement operations targeting licensed
  retailers.
● Where violations are present, conduct post-enforcement operations, including
  issuing “Notice of Violations” and citations, when appropriate.
● Conduct quarterly “shoulder tap” or other operations involving the furnishing of
  tobacco products to minors from non-commercial sources.
● Conduct weekly local tobacco retail license inspection operations.
● Conduct quarterly operations involving the sale of single cigarettes.
● Conduct quarterly operations involving the sale of tobacco products violating local
  ordinances.

The Department of Justice has allocated funding for two full-time code enforcement
officers and the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department to enforce tobacco-related
laws for the term of the agreement.

Staff recommends that the Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-011, authorizing the
acceptance and continuation of the California Department of Justice Tobacco Grant
Program funds and the related agreement (A-8670), approve two full-time code
enforcement officer positions and direct the City Manager, or her designee, to execute
any documents related to the agreement, acceptance, and continuation of the grant.

FISCAL IMPACT

$793,710; this grant is available on a reimbursement basis, with $252,708 allocated for
fiscal year 2023-24 and $264,162 and $276,300, respectively, for fiscal year 2024-25
and fiscal year 2025-26.

PURPOSE
This Memorandum of Understanding (“MOU”) is entered into by the Department of Justice (“DOJ”)
and the City of Palmdale Public Safety Department (“Grantee”), for the purpose of disbursing grant
funds to Grantee for reimbursement of expenditures in compliance with the California Code of
Regulations and the Fiscal Year 2023-24 Grantee Handbook.

Commencing January 1, 2023, the California Code of Regulations, Title 11, Division 1, Chapter 5:
Department of Justice Tobacco Grant Program (“TGP Regulations”) shall govern the policies and
procedures of the Tobacco Grant Program.

The TGP Regulations, Request for Proposals, Grantee Handbook (dated March 2023), and Summary of
Award document are hereby incorporated by reference into this MOU. Grantee will expend funds for
the purposes identified in the approved Summary of Award document. Reimbursements are to be
funded under the California Healthcare, Research and Prevention Tobacco Tax Act of 2016, approved
by the voters as Proposition 56.

COST REIMBURSEMENT
DOJ agrees to reimburse Grantee in arrears, for Grantee’s actual expenditures in performing the
project or scope of work included in the approved Summary of Award document. Reimbursements will
be made upon receipt of invoices from Grantee and approval of the invoices by DOJ, in accordance
with the reimbursement procedures set forth in the TGP Regulations and Grantee Handbook.

BUDGET CONTINGENCY CLAUSE
It is mutually agreed, if the Budget Act of the current fiscal year and/or any subsequent years covered
under the MOU does not appropriate sufficient funds, the MOU shall be of no further force and effect.
In the event this situation occurs, DOJ shall have no liability to reimburse/pay any funds to Grantee, or
to furnish any other considerations under this MOU. As well, Grantee shall not be obligated to
continue performing the provisions of this MOU, for which the Grantee would have been reimbursed.

If funding for any fiscal year is reduced or deleted in the Budget Act for purposes of this MOU, DOJ
shall have the option to either cancel this MOU with no liability occurring to DOJ, or offer an
addendum to the Grantee to reflect the reduced amount.

PROJECT BREACH-TERMINATION
Failure of a Grantee to comply with this MOU or the TGP Regulations shall be treated by DOJ as a
breach of contract. If an act of noncompliance occurs, DOJ may take actions described within the TGP
Regulations, including termination. DOJ may terminate this MOU and be relieved of any obligation to
disburse grant funds to Grantee should Grantee fail to perform the scope of work at the time and in
the manner provided in this MOU.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council approve the City’s 2024 State and Federal
Legislative Platform (Legislative Platform) to promote Palmdale’s legislative priorities.

BACKGROUND

Active legislative engagement is necessary to protect and enhance the interests of
Palmdale’s residents and businesses. The City Council has identified the importance of
having an approved and current Legislative Platform to improve the organization’s
legislative efficiency and effectiveness. The City Council last approved the City’s
Legislative Platform on February 5, 2019.

DISCUSSION

Approving an updated Legislative Platform provides the framework to continue
addressing the fundamental issues deemed by the City Council as imperative to the City
and community while delivering a proactive approach to deal with the rapidly changing
nature of state and federal legislative and policy issues. The development of the
Legislative Platform allows for a guiding blueprint to engage in proactive advocacy efforts
at the state and federal levels. The Legislative Platform will form a cornerstone of the
City’s advocacy and legislative priorities in four strategic areas that staff will utilize to
advance City initiatives: Building Culture & Community, Economic Vitality & Innovation,
Social Unity, and Transportation & Infrastructure.

City staff works collaboratively with the City’s contracted state lobbying firm, Gonsalves
& Son, and federal lobbying firms, Lincoln Park Group, LLC and Townsend Public Affairs,
Cal Cities (formerly League of California Cities), and the California Contract Cities
Association (CCCA) to monitor and track legislation impacting local governments. These

and can be revised and improved upon as needed. It will be reviewed annually in

  1
 INTRODUCTION

The Legislative Platform for the City of Palmdale was developed utilizing the City Council’s
goals and priorities, which apply to legislative priorities at both State and Federal levels of
government. These legislative priorities fall under the Council’s four strategic focus priority
areas that the City will work to advance in 2024 and beyond: Building Culture & Community,
Economic Vitality & Innovation, Social Unity and Transportation & Infrastructure.

The City strongly promotes local control of cities. It will support or oppose legislation based on
whether it impacts local control over City revenues, land use, community development, and
other municipal actions.

This document describes focus areas; however, due to the vigorous nature of the policy-
making process, additional issues are likely to arise throughout the legislative session. The
overarching principles in this Legislative Platform shall guide and direct staff as these different
issues require action. Any policy issues not addressed in this platform will be communicated to
the City Council for consideration before the City acts on that item.

  2
   BUILDING CULTURE & COMMUNITY
The City of Palmdale seeks resources and tools to promote the safety of our
residents, uplift community pride through beautification programs and elevate the
community’s preparedness and resiliency.

WE SUPPORT

Beautification, Public Appearance and Environmental Health
 Support all legislation that furthers the expansion and development of tools and programs
  to deter crimes of vandalism, graffiti and illegal dumping, and investment in the aesthetics
  and physical environment of the City, including but not limited to Landscape Maintenance
  Districts (LMDs), trees, hardscapes and public art.

Public Safety
 Work with federal, state, county, and regional agencies to further legislation intended to
  facilitate public safety; to support funding through grants and other opportunities to
  enhance community-oriented policing policies and programs in the City aimed at reducing
  crime and increasing social trust; and support the development of programs that enhance
  relationship-building between law enforcement and all segments of our community.

Emergency Preparedness
 Support federal and state legislation providing funding through grants and other
  opportunities for emergency operations, hazard mitigation, and emergency response and
  recovery from natural and unnatural disasters.

Housing Improvement and Availability Program

 Support legislation that promotes, enhances, and funds the development of programs to
  encourage and assist in maintaining quality housing standards and availability to all.

Housing and Land Use Development

 Support legislation that allows the City to have local control to address the community's
  broadest and least regulated economic, land use, environmental, and permitting needs while
  expanding opportunities to build affordable housing and transit-oriented developments.

  3
 WE OPPOSE

Efforts to reprioritize public safety funding and programs

 Oppose efforts to reprogram public safety funding elsewhere without proper procedural or
  stakeholder engagement and measures that would decrease public safety services or
  increase crime.

Loss of local control

 Oppose state initiatives that would remove local control subsequently limiting diverse
  housing development in Palmdale and its spheres of influence and interfere with protecting
  residential neighborhoods.

Unrealistic Timeframes

 Oppose new legislation and mandates for unrealistic processing timeframes or conditions
  that impede housing for larger housing development projects.

Imposition of Regulatory or Statutory Requirements

 Oppose legislation that affects and impairs the administration of parks and recreation
  services and resources management, including the sale of parklands and open space and
  relaxations of park dedication fee requirements that provide no added protections or
  benefits to California’s recreational consumer.

 Oppose all measures that limit, impair, or dilute the City’s ability to address housing
  standards and availability.

  4
   ECONOMIC VITALITY & INNOVATION
The City of Palmdale supports activities and opportunities that will help develop a
skilled workforce and grow the local economy through innovative programs and
incentives, including expanding the film and industrial/manufacturing industries in
the local region.

WE SUPPORT

Local Jobs

 Legislation that assists and creates comprehensive economic development strategies to
  create local jobs, including, but not limited to, mortgage-paying jobs, by targeting growing
  industries, including film, healthcare, manufacturing, industrial and warehousing,
  transportation, and technology testing facilities.

Workforce Development

 Support legislation that supports funding and initiatives that encourage and support the
  growth of workforce development, skill development, and training opportunities in the City
  and region.

 Support legislation that expands workforce development programs that encourage diversity
  in business industries serving Palmdale.

Small Business Development

 Seek and support legislation that promotes financial support through grants and other
  funding opportunities to support and educate small businesses.

Economic Development Investment Incentive Programs

 Advocate for legislation that expands resources that modernizes existing economic
  development programs, including Enhanced Infrastructure Financing Districts (EIFD).

Film & Tourism

 Support and initiate legislation to enhance the economy and create jobs in all creative
  industries, especially film and tourism opportunities.

Exploring New Industries

 Advocate for legislation that proposes and enhances programs and funding to create jobs
  and develop a workforce in high-tech innovation and green technology industries.

  5
 WE OPPOSE

By-right legislation

 Oppose legislation that limits the City’s discretionary review processes for local
  development projects or economic development opportunities.

 Oppose legislation that interferes, limits, or eliminates the decision-making authority of local
  municipalities regarding local land use or economic development opportunities.

 Oppose any legislation limiting the expansion of current industries operating in the
  community.

Unfunded Mandates

 Oppose the imposition of unfunded or less-than-funded mandates on local governments,
  regardless of the form, source, or policy, including administrative, legislative, and
  interpretive sources, regardless of the governmental or other source.

  6
   SOCIAL UNITY
The City of Palmdale seeks funding and supports opportunities to maximize
sustainability initiatives that address connectivity, homelessness and mental
health, public accessibility, and environmental sustainability.

WE SUPPORT

Broadband

 Support legislation supporting funding to advance Broadband City-wide to all residents
  regardless of income status.

Environmental Sustainability

 Support legislation supporting funding for clean transportation, net zero energy use in
  future construction projects, and a localized organics treatment facility.

Housing

 Support legislation supporting increased funding through administrative and housing
  programs that create diverse housing options in Palmdale, including affordable, veterans,
  low-income, senior, and workforce housing.

SAVES Program

 Advocate for legislation funding resources for the South Antelope Valley Emergency
  Services (SAVES) program.

Homelessness and Mental Health

 Support legislation enhancing regional and City-driven solutions to address homelessness
  through crisis response, mental health evaluation and treatment, housing, homeless
  outreach teams, and state and regional funding for mental health crisis units.

 Support legislation providing for the expansion of laws, allowing for increased guardianship
  control and health supervision of those with mental illness and recognizing mental illness
  and addiction as a contributor to chronic homelessness.

Domestic Violence Programs

 Support legislation providing funding through grants and other opportunities to address
  domestic violence issues, including funding for the development of shelter and program
  services.

  7
 Illegal Drug Prevention and Treatment

 Support legislation funding programs targeting the education, prevention, and treatment of
  the use of illegal drugs and legal drug misuse.

Public Accessibility

 Support legislation funding through grants and other opportunities that enhance public
  facilities and programs, including recreational trails, parks, libraries, and museums, to make
  them accessible to all populations.

WE OPPOSE

Regional Housing Need Assessment (RHNA) Mandate

 Oppose legislation that proposes to change the Regional Housing Need Assessment
  (RHNA) from a planning process to a production requirement.

 Oppose legislation that penalizes a city or local government if identifiable RHNA units are
  not constructed or are delayed by actions of third parties.

  8
   TRANSPORTATION & INFRASTRUCTURE
Palmdale seeks funding and opportunities to promote the transformation of transit,
water, and technological advancements in our community.

WE SUPPORT

High Desert Corridor Alignment

 Support the implementation and construction of the High Desert Corridor Alignment project
  and support or initiate legislation to advance the same.

Palmdale Airport Development

 Vigorously support the mission of Air Force Plant 42 while concurrently working with local,
  state, and federal agencies to bring commercial passenger air service to the Palmdale
  Airport.

Recycled Water Infrastructure

 Support the development of recycled water infrastructure throughout the City and initiate
  legislation to further the same.

Technology Infrastructure

 Support legislation and policies oriented toward advancing and constructing technology
  infrastructure throughout the City, including broadband and wireless communications that
  support Smart Cities initiatives.

 Support or initiate legislation and policies furthering local oversight and control of
  technology placement and franchises.

Palmdale Boulevard

 Support legislation and administrative efforts that seek funding for the acquisition of
  Palmdale Boulevard from CalTrans.

Avenue M Grade Separation

 Support legislation and administrative efforts that seek funding for the Avenue M Grade
  Separation project.

 Rancho Vista Grade Separation

 Support legislation and administrative efforts that seek funding for the Rancho Vista Grade

Hydrogen Infrastructure

 Support infrastructure legislation and funding opportunities for investments in green energy
  projects, including hydrogen refueling infrastructure, to decrease the City’s carbon footprint
  while not being destructive to small businesses and the local economy.

Rail Infrastructure

 Support expansion and construction of high-speed rail infrastructure, including the
  California High-Speed Rail project and Brightline, and develop a strategy to prepare the
  local economy for project deployment.

WE OPPOSE

Regulation of Wireless Facilities

 Oppose any legislation or regulatory policy that limits local discretion to regulate wireless
  facilities, cellular communications towers, transmission sites, or other infrastructure.

 Oppose any legislation or administrative policy that opposes any City goal, initiative, or
  policy.

6)  PUBLIC HEARING
  6.1) Adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-017, a Resolution of the City Council of the
  City of Palmdale; Denying Appeal 24-0002 and upholding Planning
  Commission Resolution No. PC-2024-001 to deny General Plan Amendment
  23-0001, Zone Change 23-0002, and Specific Plan Amendment 22-001.

  Mayor Bishop made the following statement:

  "There are a lot of important issues involved in this application and there are
  several stakeholders who have real concerns in regard to this Specific Plan
  area.

  The Specific Plan is a comprehensive and integrated document, it will best
  serve everyone’s interests to take a more critical look at the land use and
  economic benefit issues.

  To responsibly accomplish our review, I move that we table this item to the next
  two council meetings and further that a sub-committee, comprised of myself
  and Councilmember Ohlsen, work with the interest of all stakeholders to ensure
  everyone benefits from our actions. The sub-committee will not want any
  separate meetings to occur without its participation to ensure the most efficient
  and comprehensive analysis of the issues."

  Mayor Bishop called for a second to his motion.

  Motion: Move to table item to the March 6, 2024 Council meeting.
  Moved by Austin Bishop, seconded by Richard J. Loa.

  Vote: Motion carried (5-0)
  Yes:  Austin Bishop, Richard J. Loa, Eric Ohlsen, Laura Bettencourt, Andrea
  Alarcón.
